prompt: A Square that extends Rectangle breaks substitutability. Write SquareSafe so it implements the provided Shape interface instead, plus a static describe(Shape). Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: The Liskov Substitution Principle says any Rectangle reference must keep working when a subclass instance is passed in. A Square that extends Rectangle cannot honour that: code that sets width 5 then height 4 and expects area 20 would get 16, because keeping the sides equal contradicts Rectangle's promise that width and height move independently. Sharing the Shape INTERFACE instead gives you all the polymorphism you actually wanted -- describe(Shape) and a Shape[] loop work on both types -- with none of the inherited promises you cannot keep. Prefer 'is substitutable for' over 'sounds like a kind of' when deciding whether to extend a class.
hints: SquareSafe stores one double side; area() is side * side, so setWidth/setHeight never enter the picture.
Write `public class SquareSafe implements Shape` -- implementing the interface, not extending Rectangle, is the whole point of the exercise.
describe is static and takes the interface type: build shape.name() + " area=" + shape.area() and let each object answer for itself.
